result: The authors generated a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas of zebrafish kidney identifying 13 major cell categories and 59 subset populations, including HSPCs, immune cells (neutrophils, macrophages, B cells, T/NK cells), and kidney structural cells, with detailed subclustering revealing 11 HSPC subsets, 23 T/NK subsets, 9 B cell subsets, 10 macrophage/myeloid subsets, and 6 neutrophil subsets.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding. The editor states the study 'characterizes the composition and immune diversity of the zebrafish kidney...with convincing single-cell transcriptomic data.' One reviewer notes 'Their analyses identified expected populations but also revealed new hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC),' and another describes the atlas as 'one of the most comprehensive investigations on this subject to date.' No concerns are raised about the cell type identification or classification.

result: The kidney cell populations displayed differential responses to SVCV infection, with significant changes in abundance across multiple cell types: increases in macrophage/myeloid cells, certain neutrophil subsets (N0, N2, N3), NK/NKT cells, Th2-like and Th17 cells, cycling HSPCs (H1, H3, H4), and germinal center B cells; and decreases in other neutrophil subsets (N1, N4), Th1 cells, Tregs, CD8+ CTLs, immature/mature B cells (B0), and various HSPC progenitor subsets (H0, H2, H6, H7, H8, H9).
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge these findings. One reviewer states 'Their analyses show that HSPCs in kidney can respond to virus infection differentially,' and another notes 'these cell populations exhibited distinctive responses to viral infection.' The editor confirms 'key findings suggest...hematopoietic stem cells in zebrafish may exhibit trained immunity.' The comprehensive data on cell proportion changes is presented without methodological concerns from reviewers.

result: HSPCs exhibited extensive reactivity to viral infection, and trained immunity could be effectively induced in certain HSPC subsets (particularly H0) upon SVCV vaccination followed by challenge, as evidenced by enhanced proliferation, increased abundance (H0 surged from 19.87% to 41.43% in vaccinated+infected group), and upregulation of immune-related genes in vaccinated zebrafish compared to naive infected fish.
evaluation: This finding is explicitly highlighted by reviewers as a key contribution. The editor states 'hematopoietic stem cells in zebrafish may exhibit trained immunity, which are the unique features of the fish immune system.' One reviewer notes the study shows HSPCs 'can be trained to recognize the same infection,' and another states the investigation 'revealed that HSPCs manifest positive reactivities to viral infection, indicating the effective induction of trained immunity in select HSPCs.' No concerns are raised about this interpretation.

result: The zebrafish kidney functions as a secondary lymphoid organ capable of generating complete adaptive immune responses, as demonstrated by the presence of diverse APCs and effector T and B cells, their pronounced activation and proliferation upon SVCV challenge, upregulation of CD154/CD40, antigen-induced AID expression, and somatic hypermutation in IgM+ B cells, with responses comparable to those in the spleen.
evaluation: This major conclusion is explicitly endorsed by all reviewers. The editor states 'key findings suggest that zebrafish kidney is a secondary lymphatic organ,' and one reviewer notes the authors 'argue that zebrafish kidney can serve as a secondary immune organ.' Another reviewer states the study 'unveiled the capacity for the generation of antigen-stimulated adaptive immunity within the kidney, suggesting a role for the zebrafish kidney as a secondary lymphoid organ.' The findings are described as providing 'new and valuable insights' with no methodological concerns raised.

result: The study identified various HSPC progenitor populations including NK progenitors (H5), myeloid progenitors (H6), erythrocyte progenitors (H7), lymphoid progenitors (H8), endothelial progenitors (H9), and thrombocyte progenitors (H10), with pseudotime trajectory and RNA velocity analyses revealing that H0-H4 clusters represent stem and early progenitors that differentiate into late progenitors responsible for erythroid, myeloid, and lymphocyte lineages, suggesting conserved hematopoietic pathways across species.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge these findings as important discoveries. One reviewer states the analyses 'revealed new hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC), even in spleen,' indicating acceptance of the novel HSPC characterization. The comprehensive nature of the atlas is praised as 'one of the most comprehensive investigations on this subject to date.' The identification of conserved hematopoietic components is implicitly supported through the overall positive reception of the work.

result: Comparative analysis revealed substantial overlapping HSPC and immune cell types between kidney and spleen, with similar cell differentiation trajectories and overall similarities in HSPCs' composition and differentiation potentials, suggesting analogous functionalities in hematopoiesis and immunity across both organs.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this comparative analysis. One reviewer specifically notes 'They compared within these experimental groups as well as kidney vs spleen,' indicating acceptance of the comparative approach. The finding that kidney profiles 'closely resemble those observed in the spleen' supports the secondary lymphoid organ conclusion, which reviewers explicitly endorse. No concerns are raised about the kidney-spleen comparison.

result: Detailed characterization of 23 T/NK cell subsets revealed diverse populations including NKT cells (T5, T17, T18), CD3lowCD4lowCD8low early DP T cells (T0), CD8+ cytotoxic subsets (T1, T2, T8, T9, T15), Th1 cells (T3) with dual helper/cytotoxic potential, multiple NK subsets with varying CD11b/CD27 expression patterns (T6, T7, T10, T13, T19, T20, T21), γδ T cells (T11), Th17 cells (T12), CD4+IgM+ dual expressers (T14), Tregs (T16), and Th2-like cells (T21) expressing faslg.
evaluation: This detailed T/NK cell characterization is part of the comprehensive atlas that reviewers praise. The editor notes the study provides 'convincing single-cell transcriptomic data of hematopoietic cells and immunocytes,' and one reviewer describes it as 'one of the most comprehensive investigations on this subject to date.' The identification of expected and novel populations is acknowledged without methodological concerns.

result: Nine B cell subsets were identified including immature/mature B cells (B0, B3), IgM+IgD+ B cells (B1), pro/pre B cells (B2, B7), plasma cells (B4), germinal center B-like cells (B5) expressing AID and proliferation markers, activated B cells/plasmablasts (B6) with potential regulatory B cell characteristics, and B1-like cells (B8) including IgM+TCRβ+ dual expressers, with pseudotime analysis revealing differentiation trajectories and evidence that B0 cells undergo severe cell death upon SVCV infection.
evaluation: The B cell characterization is part of the comprehensive atlas that reviewers explicitly endorse. One reviewer notes the study 'meticulously constructed a comprehensive atlas delineating hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC) and immune-cell types,' which includes these B cell subsets. The finding of cell death in B0 cells is supported by pathway analysis data, and no concerns are raised about these interpretations.

result: Ten macrophage/myeloid subsets were characterized including M1-typical macrophages (M0, M1, M7) expressing inflammatory markers, APC macrophages (M2, M5) with antigen presentation genes, M2-typical macrophages (M3, M8) expressing anti-inflammatory markers, macrophage-isg15 population (M4) with interferon-inducible genes, eosinophil-like cells (M6), and dendritic cells (M9) encompassing classical DCs, plasmacytoid DCs, and C1q+ DCs.
evaluation: This macrophage/myeloid characterization is part of the comprehensive immune cell atlas that reviewers praise. The editor confirms the study provides 'convincing single-cell transcriptomic data of hematopoietic cells and immunocytes.' The identification of diverse macrophage subsets and their functional characterization is accepted without methodological concerns as part of the overall comprehensive analysis.

result: Six neutrophil subsets (N0-N5) were identified with distinct functional enrichments: N0 in C-type lectin receptor pathway and innate antiviral responses, N1 in endocytosis, N3 in oxidative phosphorylation and interferon-mediated antiviral responses, N4 in MAPK signaling, and N5 in cell cycle processes.
evaluation: The neutrophil subset characterization is part of the comprehensive cellular atlas that reviewers explicitly endorse. One reviewer notes the manuscript is 'well written and a pleasure to read,' and the editor confirms the data is 'convincing.' The functional pathway enrichment analysis for neutrophil subsets is presented as part of the detailed characterization without raising reviewer concerns.

result: Multiple interferon genes (ifng1-1, ifng1-2, ifnphi1, ifnphi2, ifnphi3) showed cell-type-specific expression patterns before infection and were notably upregulated after SVCV infection, with ifnphi1 showing the most significant upregulation; six interferon-stimulated genes (isg15, CR318588.1, zgc:152791/ifi27.2, ifi45/ifi27.1, CR318588.2, CR318588.3) displayed the strongest responsiveness to SVCV infection across almost all cell types, suggesting conserved roles in IFN-associated immunity across vertebrate evolution.
evaluation: This interferon response characterization is part of the antiviral immunity findings that reviewers explicitly acknowledge. The editor states the study provides 'new and valuable insights into the antiviral response in teleost fish.' One reviewer notes the findings are 'important and interesting.' The RT-qPCR validation of key interferon-stimulated genes strengthens these findings, and no concerns are raised about the interferon response data or interpretation.

result: Viral sgRNAs were predominantly detected in macrophage/myeloid cells (clusters 3 and 9), indicating that macrophage/myeloid cells are the prevailing cell types supporting productive viral replication in zebrafish kidney.
evaluation: This finding about viral tropism is part of the comprehensive analysis of viral infection responses that reviewers acknowledge. The editor confirms the study provides insights into 'the antiviral response in teleost fish,' which implicitly includes understanding which cells support viral replication. The viral RNA detection data is presented without methodological concerns from reviewers.

result: Background claims establishing that vertebrate kidneys have conserved roles in waste excretion and osmoregulation, fish kidney is a functional ortholog of mammalian bone marrow serving as a hematopoietic hub, teleost fish possess fundamental innate and adaptive immune components, fish lack bone marrow and lymph nodes but have the head kidney as a primary hematopoietic site, and fish lack antibody class-switch recombination but retain AID expression.
evaluation: These are established background facts in the field that reviewers implicitly accept by not questioning them. The editor's statement that the kidney is 'the immune organ equivalent to human bone marrow' confirms acceptance of this established knowledge. These background claims provide context for the novel findings and are not contested by reviewers.
